name: Noble Oguamanam Eberechukwu
missingPieces: Decoy misidentified as MD5 (the safe construct is the hash_equals constant-time HS256 verify branch). SQLi CVSS uses A:H (9.8) where A:N (~9.1) is correct. NDPA Section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk) omitted.
feedback: Strong, evidence-led capstone that catalogues essentially all ten findings. On D1 you nailed the SQL injection (A03, CWE-89) with both the concatenated query line and the 02:15:31 admin' OR '1'='1 capture, the stored XSS (CWE-79, 02:18:47), the path traversal (CWE-22, 02:24:02), the open redirect (CWE-601, 02:21:13), XXE (CWE-611), no-expiry (CWE-613), and the cookie flags (CWE-614), each with a CWE and an evidence line, which is exactly the standard. The one real D1 miss is the decoy: you labelled F9 MD5 as the decoy, but unsalted MD5 is a genuine finding (CWE-916), and the actual safe construct you were meant to identify and prove safe is the JWT verify branch that uses hash_equals(), a constant-time compare, so the real bugs there are alg:none and the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret, not the comparison. You lost the six decoy points because of that. D2 is excellent: the chain runs recon 02:14:08, enumeration, SQLi 02:15:31, the 312-row harvest 02:16:04, XSS 02:18:47, redirect 02:21:13, file read 02:24:02 with the parallel XXE, and exfil, each hop reconciled to a capture line with a verbatim payload, and you carried the senior insight that the forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service as a scope change. The one vector slip is the SQLi: you scored CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H at 9.8, but the auth bypass does not touch availability, so it should be A:N for about 9.1. Your impact work was the right instinct, 312 customers and roughly 63 million naira with assumptions stated rather than a bare number. D3 is the standout: a CFO-readable executive summary that ends on customers, naira, and the 72-hour duty, a real threat model with the /api/v1/internal lateral path, remediation ordered by risk-reduction per hour rather than by CVSS, and two concrete stopgaps with log fields and false-positive estimates. D4 answers all four prompts in a clear first-person voice, refuses the journalist, keeps the colleague evidence to documented fact, and files the NDPC notification regardless of the manager, citing ISC2 Canon 4 and NDPA Section 40 tied to the 312 customers, though you should have added Section 41 for notifying the data subjects on high risk. The single most important fix is to identify the safe construct correctly: prove the hash_equals HS256 branch sound at the mechanism level and keep alg:none and the hardcoded secret as the real JWT bugs.
